answerNotes.DEN: A den is an animal's sheltered place. In Daniel's story it names the enclosure holding the lions.
answerNotes.KING: King can mean a ruler or a face card representing one. In a card deck, it belongs to a suit rather than ruling a country.
answerNotes.NIGHT: Night is the dark part of the daily cycle. Dusk is the fading-light period around the approach of night.
answerNotes.STONE: Stone is a piece of natural rock. A slab is a relatively flat piece, while gravel consists of many smaller pieces.
answerNotes.ANGEL: Angel means a heavenly messenger in the Bible stories. Decorative angel figures are representations rather than the story characters themselves.
answerNotes.CALL: Call can mean telephone contact or saying a name aloud. Both uses involve trying to get someone's attention.
answerNotes.VOICE: A voice is the sound produced when someone speaks or sings. A speaker is the device that reproduces the sound on a call or recording.
answerNotes.DANIEL: Bible man who survived a night among lions. This scene follows Daniel 6; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.LION: Large cat with a mane on the male. This scene follows Daniel 6; the passage gives the story's context.

answerNotes.KING: King can mean a ruler or a face card representing one. In a card deck, it belongs to a suit rather than ruling a country.
answerNotes.ROBE: A robe is a loose outer garment. In a Bible story it is clothing, not a separate kind of blanket or tablecloth.
answerNotes.SCEPTER: A scepter is a ceremonial staff representing royal authority. In Esther's story, the extended golden scepter signals that she may approach.
answerNotes.FEAST: A feast is a large celebratory meal. The meal's role depends on its story, such as welcoming a guest or celebrating a return.
